topic: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles
title: From Nowhere? System Momentum Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Jump off a boat and the boat slides back. Push off a friend on skates and you both roll away. At the ice rink, Diya sees two skaters at rest push off each other and glide apart. Nobody pushed from outside. So where did all that momentum come from? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the linear momentum of a system of particles.

On a live motion notebook two skaters push apart while the readout tracks each momentum and the total, and a graph shows the two lines spreading while the total stays flat on zero. A slow-mo replay freezes the push: equal and opposite inside forces give equal and opposite momenta. We derive P = MV and dP/dt = F external step by step, see link by link why the lighter skater glides faster, compare an inside push with an outside push side by side, and find the centre of mass velocity of three balls. Then the exam trap (zero total momentum does not mean nothing moves), an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
